slot_note: Batch 3 forecasting slot (numbered from seed FC09); v1's irrigation-district world and v2's levee and flood-frequency world are closed, identities in lineage. v3 moves to another client domain (energy-systems-utilities / load-forecasting): a cooperative's substation planning peak with conservation voltage reduction on every feeder.
niche: a member-owned electric cooperative's 2027 to 2031 summer planning peaks at one distribution substation once conservation voltage reduction runs on all its feeders, and the load it must transfer each summer to stay within the substation's firm rating, the voltage cut's effect read from a 2025 week-on, week-off pilot on three feeders
analyst_test: A strong planner who reads every rule fits the planning criteria's weather line to five summers, grows it to 2027, sees that the 2027 operating plan runs a 3 per cent voltage cut on every feeder and applies the pilot's voltage-cut effect as the pilot measured it on average, about 1.9 per cent of load; the 2027 planning peak falls under the 104.0 MW firm rating and no load moves, where the cut's effect on the hottest afternoons is about 1.0 per cent and 1.0 MW must move.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a substation's summer planning peak, a distribution planner's weather-normalised forecast of the hourly load at the design temperature, here with conservation voltage reduction running: how far a voltage cut lowers load depends on what the load is made of, and on the hottest afternoons air-conditioner compressors, which draw about constant power whatever the voltage, carry most of it; a swap to another field's nouns loses the voltage-dependence of the load that sets the answer.
layer1: weather station clock in UTC against local-time SCADA
pilot switches made late or missed
feeder labels as current assignment only
meter multipliers held in another system

spine.file: the cooperative's SCADA historian export of hourly feeder loads (five summers)

driver: An operating change's relief on a planning peak is the relief it gives under the peak's own conditions; measured in a trial switched week on, week off against unswitched peers, the relief shrinks as the load's make-up turns toward the parts the change cannot reduce, so the trial's average relief, carried to the peak, overstates it and the forward peak comes out low.
driver_concrete: Conservation voltage reduction lowers a feeder's load by its voltage-sensitive part; on the hottest afternoons constant-power air-conditioner compressors carry most of Dunraith's load, so the 2025 pilot's average reduction (about 1.9 per cent) overstates the roughly 1.0 per cent the 3 per cent cut gives at the 101 F planning peak, which the pilot feeders show against the unswitched feeders only on the pilot's hottest afternoons.
stump: A competent planner applies the pilot's average voltage-cut effect to the weather-normalised peak and files no 2027 transfer (a 2027 planning peak of about 104 MW), when the effect at the design temperature, read from the pilot feeders against the unswitched feeders on the hottest afternoons, is about 1.0 per cent and 1.0 MW must move.

differentiation.task164: task164 adds a joining intermittent load at the moments a shared peak is set; here no load joins: an operating change on every existing feeder lowers load by a share that falls as the load turns to constant-power air conditioning, read from a switched pilot against unswitched feeders on the hottest afternoons.
differentiation.task173: task173 rejected adding back load that large customers shed against a coincident-peak charge; here nothing is shed or added back: the voltage cut's relief at the planning peak is measured from a week-on, week-off pilot against comparison feeders at the peak's own temperatures.
differentiation.task138: The slot's architectures v1 (an irrigation order's root-zone start state) and v2 (a flood record restored through a second gauge) share no world, file or mechanism with v3: a voltage-reduction effect estimated at the planning peak's conditions from a switched pilot.

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces has to start every trace from the store each unit actually holds at the forecast date, rebuilt from each unit's own last recorded replenishment and the observed drawdown since; starting every trace full, letting each trace inherit the store its own past year left, or rebuilding the store from the model's replenishment rule instead of the record each understates it, because most units were last replenished weeks before the rule would have replenished them and the interval since was dry.
lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-14 at round 2: the 10/10 audit (COMPLIANT_WEAK) found the start-state fork and the stump the same gap (no filed sentence fixed the 1 February state; the judge's DETERMINISTIC was conditional on it), the decisive step visible (the 64,887-row orders file the one large non-distractor file the default path never read, Table 1's November to January coefficients, the weather to 31 January 2027; the judge and the reader both found it unprompted) and Ask A's meter chaining crackable through the shop log's registers; never on the portal

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces starts every trace from the store each unit holds at the forecast date, and that store has to be rebuilt by running each unit's recorded replenishments through the season from the last time the record shows it full, because units run at a working deficit are replenished by about what they used and never return to full: taking each unit's last recorded replenishment as a refill, starting every trace full or spinning the model up on its own refill rule each leaves out the deficit the operation carried into the off-season.
lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-15 at round 3: the rule 3 audit (VERDICT FAIL, rule application) found the start state the procedure's own daily balance (WOP 3.1 to 3.3) executed on the 2026 delivery record at Table 4's efficiency, which the table defined as the share of delivered water the root zone receives, so the filed sentences executed word for word gave the golden (215,000) with nothing left to estimate; that route is now round 3's default path; never on the portal

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces starts from each unit's store at the forecast date, rebuilt by running each unit's recorded inputs through the balance at the share of each input that reaches the store; the design share is not the record's, and only the monitored units' readings through the input season identify the record's share, because at the forecast date every monitored unit's store is the same under any share: carrying the design share, the monitored units' end-point readings, their offset or their share of capacity to the unmonitored units misstates the units replenished late in the season, on which the order turns.

lineage.driver: A forward design value is fitted to a record whose large events were partly absorbed by a storage that has since been removed, so the record's upper tail understates the forward one; the present behaviour shows only in the few large events since the removal, and carrying a longer unaffected upstream record through that present relation restores a series the design value can be fitted to.
